summary:
Could you design a rocket when every kilogram and every dollar matters? A physics-based build-and-launch game made for the Space Apps Challenge.

NASA has given you one job: design a rocket capable of exploring farther into space than any rocket before it. You have a budget, a set of real materials and parts, and a world that applies real physics to whatever you build — every choice you make trades cost against performance.

The shop opens with Steel, Titanium, Nickel Superalloy, Aluminium and Engine parts to choose from. Placing material is simple, and the shape you draw decides what you get:

Double-click two points to draw a structural line between them.

Click four points normally to place a filled polygon panel.

Double-click the first point, then click the remaining two.

Each part's weight comes from its density and size, so cost and mass trade off against each other on every piece you place — a dense, cheap steel beam flies differently than a light, pricey titanium one.

Starting budget of $65,000,000; every part is charged against it
Gravity and ground collision act on every part you place
Fuel tank holds up to 131 units, and the engine burns it while firing
Run out of fuel and the rocket crashes

Make sure to save your rocket before you launch
else your rocket will be lost forever
